title: Pay and the road trip from Boston to Sioux City
summary: Hired at $25 a week in Boston, he travels west by car with the band, photographed in uniform at Buffalo, and reaches Sioux City wide-eyed.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: A little more elaboration on the Dan Murphy days -- as I remember, we were all young boys, naturally, it was the first territorial bands they used to have, and when I joined the band, that was a big thing; we talked it over at home and my father said I could go. I think I went at $25 a week, which in those days was a lot of money, and if I sent my
grandmother $8 or $10 home, well, that was in the days when you could get steaks -- in Kansas City you could get a steak dinner for 20 or 25¢.
But what town were you in -- you mentioned Kansas City now.
Oh, Boston? Dan Murphy -- did you work in Kansas City with them?
Well, I joined in Boston, he hired me in Boston.
But did you go to Kansas City with them?
I got on the car -- they had a truck for the instruments, and two cars.

And we left Boston, and I don't know what time of year it was. I would say it was around the Spring, and the first stop we made was a few minutes in Buffalo -- this was by car in the old days; we stopped at Buffalo to have our pictures taken -- put on the uniforms, which they used for publicity, and I'll show them to you

sometime, and take the uniforms off and get back in the car -- and we haven't checked in anyplace yet. And from Buffalo, the next stop we made was Sioux City, Iowa. Now that's a lot of traveling -- that was two or three days in those days by auto. And I never slept a wink; I was never so thrilled in my life. I was traveling and watching the countryside -- I'd never seen corn and hogs on the way.
